title: DW-MT328-DurabilityProofSuite
group: DW Durable workspace volumes and handoff
clause: Adversarial durability proofs as named regression tests: VMM kill mid-write + reattach, wsl --shutdown host-teardown survival (operator-gated), GC negative proofs, quota-never-deletes proof; UserManual entries for the volume/handoff surface + manual self-consistency test; three-tier diagnostics posture recording

scope.summary:
GOAL: Close the DW family with an ADVERSARIAL proof suite that attacks the durability and GC-safety claims the earlier MTs made, plus the consolidated UserManual surface and the three-tier diagnostics posture record. The stance is the research catalogs' testing doctrine (reconciler catalog P21: named crash-injection regression cases for the exact field failure modes - e.g. flintlock #326's 'spawn succeeded, process died' - kept forever as named tests): every claim gets a test that tries to BREAK it, and the broken-world scenarios from the durable-volumes catalog (P1 virtiofsd death, P8 ignored flush, P9 delta corruption, P15 GC race, P16/P17/P18 fencing) each map to at least one named proof. This MT adds no new product capability; it hardens, documents, and posture-records what MT-321..327 built. Where earlier MTs already shipped a proof (e.g. MT-323's harness, MT-326's invariant tests), this MT promotes them into the named durability suite and adds the scenarios no single MT owned end-to-end.

EXPECTED DIFF SHAPE: a dedicated test module family src/backend/handshake_core/tests/dw_durability_suite/ (or the crate's test-layout equivalent) with named tests; a small operator-gated harness for the wsl --shutdown scenario; UserManual consolidation for the whole volume/handoff surface + the manual self-consistency test; a diagnostics posture record (typed Rust structure serialized into the test evidence, not a .md file) enumerating the three-tier disposition of every DW surface. No production-code changes except test seams explicitly needed and agreed via the earlier MTs' emitter/trait seams.

DETAILED SPEC:
1. Named adversarial proofs (all against real resources - Spec-Realism Gate is the point of this MT; every test name below is contract surface):
   dw328_kill_vmm_midwrite_volume_survives_delta_discarded: boot a real VM (own child) with delta + named volume; guest starts a sustained write stream to the volume AND to its delta-backed rootfs; host SIGKILLs the CH child MID-WRITE (no fsync ack wait - harsher than MT-323's harness); reattach path runs MT-323's unclean gate; PROVE: named volume file intact and mountable, last-fsynced data present, delta discarded cleanly with generation increment, no partial delta reused, binding rows consistent (kill only the session-spawned CH child per [GLOBAL-INSPECT-014]).
   dw328_wsl_shutdown_host_teardown_survival (OPERATOR-GATED): wsl --shutdown tears down the entire WSL utility VM - other WSL processes included - so this harness NEVER runs unattended: it is a separate ignored-by-default harness gated on HANDSHAKE_ALLOW_WSL_SHUTDOWN_TEST=1 AND an interactive operator confirmation, documented as a manual step per [GLOBAL-BUILD-053/054]. Sequence: write + guest fsync -> graceful-close through step 3 (snapshot) -> operator (or gated harness) runs wsl --shutdown -> restart WSL -> reattach; PROVE: named volume survives the utility-VM teardown (research Area-1 WSL caveat: the second flush layer WSL-VHDX->NTFS is not under our control - the recorded result documents observed behavior and its bounds, and the test asserts the volume's fsynced state, not unflushed host-cache state).
   dw328_gc_cannot_select_leased (negative): construct every fenced_object_kind under active leases, run full sweep cycles past grace; PROVE zero candidates for leased objects (re-running MT-326's proof inside the suite with richer object mix).
   dw328_gc_cannot_select_unpromoted (negative): unleased, unreferenced, un-promoted volumes/blobs aged past every timer; full sweep cycles; PROVE the candidate query returns nothing and a tampered hand-inserted candidate is refused at the delete layer (both MT-326 layers exercised through the public seams, not by SQL shortcuts).
   dw328_quota_pressure_never_deletes: drive a workspace over quota with un-promoted work; PROVE writes block with typed QuotaExceeded, pressure events emit, and a full sweep afterward deletes zero bytes of that workspace's data (byte-level before/after comparison of the volume tree).
   dw328_export_promote_gc_end_to_end: the happy-path lifecycle as one integration proof: provision -> work -> export -> promote -> detach workspace -> release leases -> age past grace -> sweep; PROVE only the promoted-and-now-unreferenced delta/scratch objects the contract allows are collected, the promoted bundle blobs remain resolvable in CAS, and every FR-EVT-DW-* event MT-327 defines appears in order.
   dw328_crash_between_gc_commit_and_unlink: re-run MT-326's orphan-not-phantom proof inside the suite.
2. UserManual consolidation + self-consistency test: consolidate the per-MT manual entries (MT-321..327 target_entries) into a coherent 'Workspace volumes and handoff' manual section covering: base images/CAS, named volumes + /hsk-volume convention, flush gate + unclean recovery, outbox + bundles + provenance, promotion + denial evidence, GC/leases/quotas/alerts, DW Volumes panel usage - written for a no-context model per [GLOBAL-BUILD-002..012] (purpose, workflows, commands, inputs/outputs, failure modes, recovery steps). SELF-CONSISTENCY TEST: a named test walks the manual's machine-checkable claims (commands exist, env vars honored, author_id targets present, table/view names real, event kinds real) and fails on drift - the manual becomes a tested artifact, not prose hope. Manual version bump per HBR-MAN-004.
   Manual-claims extraction convention: the manual's machine-checkable claims are maintained as a typed claims list in the test module (claim kind + expected symbol/command/target), so the self-consistency test compiles against reality; prose paragraphs are not parsed.
3. Three-tier diagnostics posture recording: a typed PostureRecord { surface: String, flight_recorder: Disposition, internal_diagnostics: Disposition, palmistry: Disposition, reason: String } serialized (JSON) into the suite's evidence output under ../Handshake_Artifacts/dw_durability_suite/, enumerating every DW surface (CAS, base registry, provisioning, flush gate, close orchestration, export, promotion, GC sweeper, quotas, leases, panel) and asserting in a test that (a) every surface MT-327 wired as FLIGHT_RECORDER=WIRED actually emits in the end-to-end proof, and (b) every DEFERRED disposition recorded by MT-321..326 is now either closed by MT-327 or carries a current reason - stale deferrals fail the test. This makes the hbr_int_009 tier bookkeeping itself machine-verified.
4. Suite mechanics: real-VM tests are #[ignore]-tagged for plain unit runs and executed by an explicit suite invocation (cargo test ... -- --ignored) so default CI stays fast while the MT verdict requires the full suite; each test seeds and tears down its own scratch runtime root + SurrealDB schema state; teardown uses exact-path removal of its own scratch files only (no --force, no recursive deletion of shared roots); suite evidence (timings, outcomes, screenshots from the MT-327 panel where relevant, posture record) lands under ../Handshake_Artifacts/dw_durability_suite/<run_id>/.
5. RESOURCE PRIVACY NOTE: suite fixtures create their own scratch accounts/Principals; proofs assert scope isolation as part of the end-to-end test (account B observer sees nothing of account A's lifecycle in projections, exports, or GC visibility - HBR-PRIV-004, derive_from_sources intersection semantics resource_scope.rs ~193-228); evidence files contain only scratch-account identifiers.

STEP-BY-STEP:
1. Read the shipped MT-321..327 implementations and their existing named tests on post-merge main; inventory which contract proofs already exist vs which this suite must add.
2. Build the suite skeleton + scratch-environment fixtures (runtime root, SurrealDB state, scratch accounts, real VM helpers reusing MT-322/323 test plumbing).
3. Implement the seven named adversarial proofs; wire the wsl --shutdown harness behind its env + operator gate with manual-step documentation.
4. Consolidate the UserManual section; implement the typed claims list + self-consistency test; bump manual version.
5. Implement the PostureRecord enumeration + stale-deferral assertion; generate the evidence output.
6. Run the full suite (real VM tests included; wsl --shutdown scenario as the documented operator-gated step); record all measured output and evidence under ../Handshake_Artifacts/dw_durability_suite/.
7. Hand to validation with the suite results; implementer never marks COMPLETED.

acceptance_criteria: AC-328-1: dw328_kill_vmm_midwrite_volume_survives_delta_discarded passes against a real VM: named volume intact with last-fsynced data, delta discarded with generation increment, bindings consistent; only the session-spawned CH child is killed.

AC-328-2: dw328_wsl_shutdown_host_teardown_survival exists as an operator-gated harness (env gate + interactive confirmation + manual-step documentation); when the operator runs it, the fsynced volume state survives WSL utility-VM teardown and the observed result incl. flush-layer bounds is recorded in evidence.

AC-328-3: dw328_gc_cannot_select_leased and dw328_gc_cannot_select_unpromoted pass with the full fenced-object mix, exercising both MT-326 invariant layers through public seams; both are named regressions wired into the suite permanently.
AC-328-4: dw328_quota_pressure_never_deletes proves byte-level preservation of over-quota un-promoted workspaces across full sweep cycles, alongside typed write refusal and pressure events.
AC-328-5: dw328_export_promote_gc_end_to_end passes: full lifecycle with correct FR-EVT-DW-* event ordering, promoted blobs remaining resolvable, and only contract-permitted objects collected.
AC-328-6: The consolidated 'Workspace volumes and handoff' UserManual section exists, covers all seven listed topic areas for a no-context model, and the manual version is bumped.

AC-328-7: The manual self-consistency test walks the typed claims list (commands, env vars, author_id targets, table/view names, event kinds) against reality and passes; introducing a deliberate drift in a test fixture proves it fails (meta-test).

AC-328-8: The PostureRecord evidence enumerates every DW surface across all three tiers; the stale-deferral assertion passes (all MT-321..326 FR deferrals closed by MT-327 or carrying current reasons); evidence lands under ../Handshake_Artifacts/dw_durability_suite/<run_id>/.

AC-328-9: Scope isolation is asserted inside the end-to-end proof with a second scratch account observing nothing; suite teardown removes only its own scratch files by exact path (no --force, no recursive shared-root deletion).

AC-328-10: Full suite results (including the operator-gated harness disposition) are recorded as measured output; the implementer never marks COMPLETED - the validator holds verdict authority over this MT and, through it, the DW family's durability claims.

implementation_notes: Field basis: reconciler catalog P21 (named crash-injection regressions for exact field failure modes; deterministic replay ethos without adopting a simulation runtime) applied to the durable-volumes catalog's failure inventory: P1 (sidecar death), P8 (ignored flush), P9 (delta corruption -> discard remedy), P15 (GC race), P16/P17/P18 (fencing, review, quota). Each named test cites its pattern in a test-level comment.

Process safety is absolute: kill only session-spawned CH children ([GLOBAL-INSPECT-014]); wsl --shutdown disrupts processes this session did not start, hence the env gate + interactive operator confirmation + manual-step documentation - it never runs unattended or in CI.

This MT does not fix what it finds: a failing adversarial proof is a defect routed back to the owning MT's surface through the normal defect path; patching product behavior inside the proof MT would blur the validator boundary.
The suite is the DW family's permanent regression fence: proof-target names are contract surface, and later WPs touching workspace_volumes must keep the suite green.

House rules: all Rust; real SurrealDB + real VM/disk resources per the Spec-Realism Gate (this MT exists to enforce it); scoped CARGO_TARGET_DIR and all evidence under ../Handshake_Artifacts/; disk-agnostic paths, no spaces; no --force deletes anywhere including test teardown; implementer never marks COMPLETED.
Resource privacy: scratch accounts only; the end-to-end proof carries a second-account observer asserting isolation as a first-class outcome, not an afterthought.

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.note: The end-to-end proof asserts every MT-327 FR-EVT-DW-* kind actually emits in order; the posture record machine-verifies the tier bookkeeping across the whole DW family.

Suite failures surface through normal test output plus the evidence directory; diagnostic-event assertions are included where earlier MTs wired them, else their DEFERRED reasons are re-validated by the posture test.
The suite is an operator/CI-invoked test run; its liveness is the test runner's own output. The GC-sweeper palmistry disposition it validates belongs to MT-326.

risk_if_missed: The DW family ships on happy-path proofs only: the first real VMM crash, WSL teardown, GC race, or quota panic meets untested code paths, and the durability promise the whole family exists for fails exactly when invoked - with no manual for recovery and no machine-checked record of which diagnostics were ever wired.

risks: RISK-1: Adversarial tests quietly degrade into happy-path tests (fsync before the 'mid-write' kill, mocked VM instead of real, shortened grace timers that skip the race window), keeping the suite green while the claims go unproven.
RISK-2: The wsl --shutdown harness runs unattended (CI, background agent) and tears down WSL under an operator's unrelated work.
RISK-3: A failing proof gets 'fixed' by patching product behavior inside this MT, bypassing the owning MT's validation and blurring who verified what.
RISK-4: The manual self-consistency test checks only trivial claims, certifying a manual whose operative instructions have drifted.
RISK-5: Suite teardown of scratch environments deletes shared runtime-root or SurrealDB state used by concurrent sessions.
minimum_controls: CTRL-1 (RISK-1): each adversarial test asserts its own adversity preconditions (e.g. bytes-in-flight counter nonzero at kill time; real-VM marker from the adapter handle; grace timers at contract defaults); a reviewer checklist maps each test to its claimed research failure mode.
CTRL-2 (RISK-2): double gate (env var + interactive confirmation) with no CI wiring; the harness refuses when stdin is not a TTY; documented as a manual operator step.
CTRL-3 (RISK-3): forbidden_paths bars behavioral changes; the contract routes failures back as defects; validator cross-checks the diff surface is tests+manual+evidence only.
CTRL-4 (RISK-4): the typed claims list must cover every command, env var, target id, table/view, and event kind named in the manual section; the meta-test proves drift detection actually fires.

CTRL-5 (RISK-5): fixtures create per-run scratch roots and schema-scoped SurrealDB state; teardown removes only recorded exact paths; a concurrent-run smoke test proves two suite instances do not interfere.
